candidates.attacker_control: Wiki page content (markdown source) is fully attacker-controlled by any user with page-edit rights (no admin needed). A crafted link such as an image link whose text contains a double quote plus an event handler, e.g. [x" onerror="alert(1)](http://host/a.png), flows through flexmark into JSPWikiLink.url/getText(), then into the raw string. The crafted page is stored and re-rendered for every viewer, including administrators (stored XSS).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Normal JSPWikiLink rendering is escaped (JSPWikiLinkRenderer.render uses flexmark html.attr/resolveLink, JSPWikiLinkRenderer.java:54-68) and the classic JSPWikiMarkupParser escapes text (JSPWikiMarkupParser.java:525-531) and builds DOM elements with JDOM (setAttribute/addContent, e.g. makeLink lines 297-430), so the defect is specific to the hand-built strings in the markdown post-processors. flexmark HtmlInline is proven to be emitted verbatim by this module's existing test expectations. A mitigating factor is that flexmark's default raw-HTML pass-through can already make markdown wikis XSS-prone; however, the attribute-context breakout via quotes in link text/destination is a distinct missing-escaping defect, and markdown mode never checks allowHTML. I could not execute the renderer (no code execution allowed) or read flexmark sources in this snapshot, so exact parse behavior for quotes in link destinations is reasoned from the CommonMark grammar and the rendered-string construction, not runtime-confirmed.
candidates.impact: Stored cross-site scripting on pages rendered in markdown mode: script execution in the origin of the wiki for any viewer, including administrators, enabling session/token theft and privileged actions (page deletion, permission changes, user creation). The markdown pipeline also ignores the wiki's anti-HTML default jspwiki.translatorReader.allowHTML=false used by the classic parser, so the escaping weakness exists even where raw HTML is intended to be disallowed.
candidates.prerequisites: The wiki must be configured to use the markdown parser/renderer (jspwiki.renderingManager.markupParser=org.apache.wiki.parser.markdown.MarkdownParser and jspwiki.renderingManager.renderer=org.apache.wiki.render.markdown.MarkdownRenderer), as done in jspwiki-markdown's own MarkdownRendererTest setup; the attacker needs permission to save a page containing the crafted markdown link. The link text is used for alt even when the URL is only recognized as an image link (isImageLink), so the injection does not depend on the target image existing.
candidates.root_cause: JSPWiki's flexmark post-processors hand-build HTML strings from attacker-controlled markdown link data and wrap them in flexmark HtmlInline nodes, which the renderer emits verbatim. ImageLinkNodePostProcessorState builds by string concatenation with no HTML/attribute escaping; LocalLinkNodePostProcessorState injects link.getText() as raw HtmlInline for attachment links; NodePostProcessorStateCommonOperations.makeError injects arbitrary exception text raw. Because link text and link destinations can freely contain quotes (and spaces), a wiki editor can terminate the alt/src/href attribute and inject event handlers such as onerror.
candidates.title: Stored XSS in markdown rendering: unescaped link text/URL concatenated into raw HtmlInline HTML
candidates.trace: MarkdownParser.parse (~/parser/markdown/MarkdownParser.java:50-57) -> flexmark Link node -> JSPWikiLinkNodePostProcessor.process decides the link type (~/extensions/jspwikilinks/postprocessor/JSPWikiLinkNodePostProcessor.java:61-86) -> ImageLinkNodePostProcessorState.process builds the raw img string (ImageLinkNodePostProcessorState.java:52-54) or LocalLinkNodePostProcessorState.process builds raw HtmlInline from link text (LocalLinkNodePostProcessorState.java:56-60) -> MarkdownRenderer.getString renders the document (render/markdown/MarkdownRenderer.java:46-54); flexmark emits HtmlInline nodes literally, as verified by the project's own expected outputs in jspwiki-markdown/src/test/java/org/apache/wiki/render/MarkdownRendererTest.java (e.g. testInlineImages expects an unescaped tag, and testAttachmentLink expects raw / fragments).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. flexmark 0.40.16 internals are not in the snapshot; I verified from JSPWiki source/tests that constructed HtmlInline strings reach the output verbatim, but did not run the parser/renderer to observe the quote breakout. Whether JSPWiki upstream considers raw HTML in markdown mode intended behavior is unknown; the allowHTML setting is not consulted anywhere in jspwiki-markdown (verified by search). JSP/JSPX templates are absent from the snapshot, so no JSP-level rendering path could be inspected.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot with get_source_scope (1184 root files; 1183 model-visible; 1 file excluded by sensitive-name/path filter; no oversized files; NUL-containing binaries skipped) and get_relation_scope (519 Java files parsed of 1183; partial index; 7162 symbols, 17337 edges, 26167 calls, 16660 unresolved; control-flow, data-flow and semantic resolution explicitly not implemented). I inspected security-relevant Java across jspwiki-main (auth/login/CookieAuthenticationLoginModule, auth/user XML+JDBC databases, auth/SecurityVerifier, attachment AttachmentServlet/AttachmentManager, providers, parser/JSPWikiMarkupParser+LinkParser, render, ui/CommandResolver, ajax dispatcher, ReferenceManager), jspwiki-util (XmlUtil, Serializer, FileUtil, HttpUtil, ClassUtil), and all of jspwiki-markdown (parser, renderer, link attribute providers/post-processors, tests). I did not exhaustively read every one of the 519 Java files; JSP/JSPX templates and template resources under jspwiki-war/src/main/webapp/templates are absent from the snapshot, so any JSP-level sink is outside what could be inspected.
limitations: No execution, tests or scanners were run; findings are source-evidence only and not runtime-confirmed.
JSP/JSPX files and template resources are missing from the snapshot (only admin.css remains under templates/default), so JSP-level rendering/redirect sinks could not be reviewed.

flexmark 0.40.16 is an external dependency not present in the tree; its exact escaping/HTML-emission behavior is inferred from JSPWiki code and the project's own test expectations, not from the library source.

The P1 relation index is partial and syntactic: no control/data-flow or semantic resolution, 16660 unresolved calls; index labels were treated only as navigation hints and every cited edge was verified in source text.
Configuration-dependent behavior (markdown mode, cookie authentication, HTML policy) was assessed from properties/docs only; runtime DI/profile activation is unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal via the JSPWikiUID cookie in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule (jspwiki-main/src/main/java/org/apache/wiki/auth/login/CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.java:113-150,175-215,295-312): uid from HttpUtil.retrieveCookieValue is used directly in new File(cookieDir, uid) with no validation; login() reads an arbitrary readable file and treats its contents as the principal, and clearLoginCookie deletes the resolved path.
rejected_leads.reason: Real absence of validation (CWE-22), but it requires jspwiki.cookieAuthentication=true (off by default), and the visible code never calls clearLoginCookie outside tests, so arbitrary deletion is only reachable through the missing JSP logout flow. Authentication-as-arbitrary-user needs a readable file whose entire content equals the target username, which is hard to arrange; content disclosure via the displayed principal name is limited. Kept as the second-strongest lead, not submitted because the markdown XSS has a cleaner, directly evidenced output-injection path from page content.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE through XmlUtil.parse(InputStream)/parse(String) (jspwiki-util/src/main/java/org/apache/wiki/util/XmlUtil.java:64-114) using JDOM2 SAXBuilder defaults (jdom2 2.0.5, expandEntities not disabled).
rejected_leads.reason: All callers found (DefaultFilterManager.parseConfigFile/config resource, DefaultPluginManager, EditorManager, ClassUtil mappings) read local/admin-configured classpath or property-specified files, not attacker-supplied XML, so no remote attacker-controlled input was traced to the sink.

rejected_leads.lead: Java deserialization in Serializer.deserializeFromBase64 / ReferenceManager (jspwiki-util/src/main/java/org/apache/wiki/util/Serializer.java:60-71; ReferenceManager.java:320-353,398-464).
rejected_leads.reason: ObjectInputStream.readObject is used on base64 data read from the user/group databases and on work-dir reference caches. No path was found by which an HTTP client controls those bytes (profile attributes are only mutated in code/tests; reference files are server-side), so it is an unconfirmed hardening lead rather than a traceable vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect / header injection in AttachmentServlet: nextpage is only checked for "://" by validateNextPage (AttachmentServlet.java:434-449, 303-304, 524-527), so protocol-relative targets pass; getMimeType/Content-Disposition echoes att.getFileName() (lines 269-270) after validateFileName, which strips quotes but not CR/LF (AttachmentManager.java:637-679).
rejected_leads.reason: Both are plausible CWE-601/113 primitives, but impact depends on container behavior (Tomcat redirect/header normalization) and on an upload/download success path; weaker source evidence and lower impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Plugin class loading: plugin names matching [\w\._]+ (DefaultPluginManager.java:164) are passed to ClassUtil.findClass, which first tries the fully qualified name (ClassUtil.java:103-123), then WikiPluginInfo.newPluginInstance calls newInstance() before the WikiPlugin cast (DefaultPluginManager.java:711-717, 815-841).
rejected_leads.reason: Allows constructions of arbitrary classpath classes with no-arg constructors from page markup; no gadget class with a dangerous no-arg constructor was identified in the snapshot, and compatibility checks / cast failure limit impact, so it remains speculative.

summary: Reviewed Apache JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3-SNAPSHOT (1184 files, 519 Java files; 1183 model-visible, 1 path excluded). Focused on security-relevant Java in jspwiki-main, jspwiki-util and the newer jspwiki-markdown module (auth/login, attachments, providers, parser/render, XXE/deserialization sinks, redirects/headers, class loading). One strong candidate: the JSPWiki markdown rendering pipeline builds raw HTML (flexmark HtmlInline) from unescaped, page-controlled markdown link text/destinations, yielding stored XSS in attribute context. The normal JSPWikiLink renderer escapes via flexmark's html.attr; the post-processors bypass it. Secondary leads (cookie-auth path traversal, XmlUtil XXE, Serializer deserialization, AttachmentServlet redirect/header handling) are recorded as rejected/unconfirmed.
